title: The US Barred Palestine from the UN While Admitting Iran. Eighteen Outlets Noticed the Contrast.
subtitle: Russia's RT was the one outlet to cover only half the story
body_md:
For the second consecutive year, the Trump administration denied Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas and his delegation entry visas to the United Nations General Assembly. The day after that announcement, the State Department approved travel visas for Iranian President Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Araghchi to attend the same event — despite the United States and Iran being at active war for more than six months. Eighteen outlets across 14 countries universally flagged the juxtaposition. One did not.

[RT](https://www.rt.com/news/645908-us-bars-palestinian-president-un/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=RSS) covered the Abbas denial and made no mention of the Iranian visa grant. Every other outlet in this corpus — from [BBC World](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6n8m72r13ngo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss) to [Haaretz](https://www.haaretz.com/middle-east-news/iran/2026-09-18/ty-article/u-s-approves-visas-for-iranian-president-foreign-minister-to-attend-un-meeting/000001a0-b0c4-d5b2-a9ee-b2ce27dd0000) to [The Independent](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/iran-visas-un-general-assembly-2026-b3052119.html) — anchored their coverage in the asymmetry: a wartime adversary cleared for New York while a Palestinian diplomatic delegation was blocked for the second straight year. RT, which has every incentive to amplify US-Palestinian tensions as part of its editorial posture toward Washington, stripped the Iran half out entirely — the single outlet in this corpus to do so.

The State Department's public justification cited Palestinian Authority and PLO "failure to live up to commitments," specifically including actions at the International Criminal Court and International Court of Justice. [Standard Kenya World](https://www.standardmedia.co.ke/world/article/2001558032/us-again-denies-palestinian-leader-abbas-visa-to-attend-un-assembly) provided the only full-body coverage in the corpus, giving the PA's counter-claim in detail: the PA had recently reformed its welfare payments system, allocating funds on a needs basis rather than political affiliation or prisoner status. The State Department's accusation of ICC/ICJ internationalization — "taking actions to internationalize the Israeli-Palestinian conflict including through the International Criminal Court (ICC) and International Court of Justice (ICJ), seeking to bypass negotiations" — and the PA's rebuttal appear together only in the Kenya outlet. Every other publication ran the denial without the policy substance.

[The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/us-again-denies-palestinian-leader-abbas-visa-to-attend-un-assembly/article71476349.ece) added two pieces of context that no other outlet included: Abbas was permitted to address the UNGA by video, and a UN resolution connected to the access dispute received 152 votes in favour and three against. That vote count — 152-3 — contextualizes just how isolated the US position is at the multilateral level. [The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/us-approves-visas-for-iran-president-fm-araghchi-to-attend-un-high-level-meeting-even-with-sides-at-war/article71478184.ece) also flagged that the Iranian visa grant was "unusual" given no sign of progress on Strait of Hormuz access or nuclear talks, introducing a strategic-geography dimension that the wire services and Western outlets entirely omitted.

Two US outlets split along expected partisan lines but reached the same factual starting point. [Daily Wire](https://www.dailywire.com/news/the-u-s-just-delivered-another-blow-to-the-palestinian-authority-president) framed the Abbas denial as "another blow to the Palestinian Authority President" — the only outlet to use language of deliberate punitive intent rather than bureaucratic or diplomatic decision. [CBC World](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/palestinian-visas-denied-un-general-assembly-9.7347425?cmp=rss) noted the second-consecutive-year aspect without editorializing. Italian state wire [ANSA](https://www.ansa.it/sito/notizie/mondo/nordamerica/2026/09/17/trump-verso-un-momento-cruciale-in-iran-devo-prendere-unimportante-decisione_84ccac82-6fb4-45bf-81e3-70830bcbb919.html) carried a signal absent from English-language coverage entirely: Trump saying he is approaching "un momento cruciale in Iran, devo prendere un'importante decisione" — "a crucial moment in Iran, I need to make an important decision." The Italian wire positioned the Iranian visa grant inside an impending major decision on Iran that, in this corpus, only Italian-language readers could see.

Brazil's [Folha de São Paulo](https://redir.folha.com.br/redir/online/mundo/rss091/*https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/colunas/lucia-guimaraes/2026/09/aos-81-anos-onu-atravessa-sua-maior-crise-existencial.shtml) provided the widest-angle framing in the corpus, situating both visa decisions within the UN's "greatest existential crisis at 81 years" while noting that Lula's UNGA speech on non-interference from foreign powers comes on the eve of Brazil's first-round elections. A second [Folha piece](https://redir.folha.com.br/redir/online/mundo/rss091/*https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/mundo/2026/09/lula-deve-defender-nao-interferencia-estrangeira-em-seu-ultimo-discurso-do-mandato-na-onu.shtml) connected that speech directly to Lula defending sovereignty against foreign interference on the eve of Brazil's first-round election. For Folha, the Abbas denial and the Iranian grant together are not bilateral diplomatic disputes but symptoms of an institution under sustained assault from its most powerful member.

Two country silences are notable. France, a permanent Security Council member with active stakes in both Iran nuclear diplomacy and Palestinian statehood recognition, has no outlet in this corpus. Egypt, the primary Arab mediator in Palestinian-Israeli negotiations and most directly affected by PA credibility questions, is also absent. The story of American access policy at the UN is being covered entirely without the two voices most structurally positioned to contest or complicate it.

No outlet in the 18-publication corpus found or reported a strategic rationale from Washington for granting the Iran access while denying the Palestinian. The contrast was universally noted. Its logic was universally unexplained.
